title: Multi-Domain Graph Alignment with cone_align_multiple
text: cone_align_multiple() extends CONE-Align three graph domains iteratively aligning domain chosen reference graph. algorithm repeatedly solves pairwise Procrustes/assignment problems node correspondences stabilise. vignette demonstrates workflow shared alignment_benchmark dataset.

title: Multi-Domain Graph Alignment with cone_align_multiple
code: library(manifoldalign) library(multidesign) library(multivarious) library(tibble) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2)

title: Multi-Domain Graph Alignment with cone_align_multiple
code: alignment_benchmark <- manifoldalign::alignment_benchmark multi_domains <- lapply(alignment_benchmark$domains, function(dom) {   multidesign::multidesign(dom$x, dom$design) })  multi_names <- names(multi_domains) node_counts <- vapply(multi_domains, function(dom) nrow(dom$x), integer(1))  hd_multi <- multidesign::hyperdesign(multi_domains)

title: Multi-Domain Graph Alignment with cone_align_multiple
text: reference domain (domain 1) aligned identity permutation. remaining domains evaluate often aligned pairs share latent class—, labels used optimisation serve purely diagnostic.
code: cone_multi <- cone_align_multiple(   hd_multi,   ref_idx = 1,   ncomp = 6,   sigma = 0.9,   lambda = 0.05,   solver = "linear",   max_iter = 40,   tol = 1e-3 )  str(cone_multi, max.level = 1) #> List of 10 #>  $ v            : num [1:12, 1:6] 6.16 8.33 8.12 6.02 -5.89 ... #>  $ s            : num [1:240, 1:6] 0.136 0.1405 0.0687 0.1189 0.1419 ... #>  $ sdev         : num [1:6] 0.1068 0.1008 0.0893 0.0907 0.0883 ... #>  $ preproc      : NULL #>  $ block_indices:List of 3 #>  $ assignment   :List of 3 #>  $ rotation     :List of 3 #>  $ n_domains    : int 3 #>  $ ref_idx      : num 1 #>  $ iterations   : int 3 #>  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "cone_align_multiple" "multiblock_biprojector" assignments <- cone_multi$assignment ref_labels <- multi_domains[[1]]$design$condition  accuracy_values <- vapply(seq_along(multi_names)[-1], function(idx) {   mean(ref_labels[assignments[[idx]]] == multi_domains[[idx]]$design$condition) }, numeric(1))  accuracy_tbl <- tibble(   domain = multi_names[-1],   condition_accuracy = accuracy_values )  accuracy_tbl #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   domain  condition_accuracy #>   <chr>                <dbl> #> 1 domain2              0.875 #> 2 domain3              0.85

title: Multi-Domain Graph Alignment with cone_align_multiple
code: # As with the pairwise vignette, class labels are only used for evaluation and # plotting; `cone_align_multiple()` itself is unsupervised.  score_tbl <- as_tibble(as.matrix(cone_multi$s), .name_repair = "minimal") colnames(score_tbl) <- paste0("comp", seq_len(ncol(score_tbl)))  scores <- score_tbl %>%   mutate(     domain = rep(multi_names, times = node_counts),     condition = rep(ref_labels, length(multi_names))   )   ggplot(scores, aes(x = comp1, y = comp2, colour = condition, shape = domain)) +   geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +   labs(title = "cone_align_multiple embeddings (first two components)",        x = "Component 1", y = "Component 2") +   theme_minimal()

title: Multi-Domain Graph Alignment with cone_align_multiple

title: Pairwise Graph Alignment with cone_align
text: cone_align() aligns two graph domains alternating spectral embeddings, orthogonal Procrustes rotations, linear assignment. vignette demonstrates workflow shared alignment_benchmark dataset results directly comparable alignment methods package.

title: Pairwise Graph Alignment with cone_align
code: library(manifoldalign) library(multidesign) library(multivarious) library(tibble) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2)

title: Pairwise Graph Alignment with cone_align
text: use first two domains alignment_benchmark. domain contains 80 nodes, 4-dimensional feature matrix, design data frame latent class label (condition).
code: alignment_benchmark <- manifoldalign::alignment_benchmark pair_domains <- alignment_benchmark$domains[1:2]  pair_multidesign <- lapply(pair_domains, function(dom) {   multidesign::multidesign(dom$x, dom$design) })  pair_names <- names(pair_multidesign) node_counts <- vapply(pair_multidesign, function(dom) nrow(dom$x), integer(1))  hd_pair <- multidesign::hyperdesign(pair_multidesign)

title: Pairwise Graph Alignment with cone_align
code: cone_fit <- cone_align(   hd_pair,   ncomp = 8,   sigma = 0.9,   lambda = 0.05,   solver = "linear",   max_iter = 40,   tol = 1e-3 )  str(cone_fit, max.level = 1) #> List of 7 #>  $ v            : num [1:8, 1:8] -5.72 -8.56 -7.88 -5.65 -5.88 ... #>  $ s            : num [1:160, 1:8] -0.1024 -0.0999 -0.0762 -0.0323 -0.1258 ... #>  $ sdev         : num [1:8] 0.1059 0.1034 0.0919 0.0887 0.0956 ... #>  $ preproc      : NULL #>  $ block_indices:List of 2 #>  $ assignment   : int [1:80] 75 1 31 4 21 36 77 8 2 10 ... #>  $ rotation     :List of 2 #>  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "cone_align" "multiblock_biprojector"

title: Pairwise Graph Alignment with cone_align
text: cone_align() returns permutation vector (assignment) maps nodes second domain nodes first (reference) domain. latent class labels used optimisation—consulted diagnostic see often unsupervised alignment preserves original classes.
code: assignment <- cone_fit$assignment ref_labels <- pair_multidesign[[1]]$design$condition cmp_labels <- pair_multidesign[[2]]$design$condition  condition_accuracy <- mean(ref_labels[assignment] == cmp_labels) identity_fraction <- mean(assignment == seq_along(assignment))  tibble(   metric = c("Class agreement", "Exact identity"),   value = c(condition_accuracy, identity_fraction) ) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   metric          value #>   <chr>           <dbl> #> 1 Class agreement 0.875 #> 2 Exact identity  0.262

title: Pairwise Graph Alignment with cone_align
text: aligned embeddings (cone_fit$s) stack two domains. visualise first two components draw handful matching pairs illustrate assignments.
code: # Note: class labels are only used for visual diagnostics below; `cone_align` # operates in a completely unsupervised manner and does not see `condition`.  score_tbl <- as_tibble(as.matrix(cone_fit$s), .name_repair = "minimal") colnames(score_tbl) <- paste0("comp", seq_len(ncol(score_tbl)))  scores <- score_tbl %>%   mutate(     domain = rep(pair_names, times = node_counts),     condition = rep(ref_labels, length(pair_names))   )  # pick 15 nodes to visualise correspondences set.seed(123) subset_idx <- sample(seq_len(node_counts[1]), size = 15) segment_df <- tibble(   x = scores$comp1[subset_idx],   y = scores$comp2[subset_idx],   xend = scores$comp1[node_counts[1] + assignment[subset_idx]],   yend = scores$comp2[node_counts[1] + assignment[subset_idx]] )   ggplot(scores, aes(x = comp1, y = comp2, colour = condition, shape = domain)) +   geom_point(size = 2.1, alpha = 0.85) +   geom_segment(     data = segment_df,     aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),     inherit.aes = FALSE,     colour = "grey60",     linewidth = 0.4,     alpha = 0.7   ) +   labs(title = "cone_align embeddings (first two components)",        x = "Component 1", y = "Component 2") +   theme_minimal()

title: Pairwise Graph Alignment with cone_align
text: cone_align() produces orthogonally aligned embeddings together node correspondence. benchmark pair assignments correctly match underlying class ~87.5% cases. dataset used kema gpca_align vignettes, enabling easy comparison across alignment techniques, remembering cone_align() remains class-agnostic.

title: Coupled Diagonalization across Modalities
code: bench <- manifoldalign::alignment_benchmark multi_domains <- lapply(bench$domains, function(dom) {   multidesign::multidesign(dom$x, dom$design) })  multi_names <- names(multi_domains) node_counts <- vapply(multi_domains, function(dom) nrow(dom$x), integer(1))  hd_multi <- multidesign::hyperdesign(multi_domains)

title: Coupled Diagonalization across Modalities
code: cd_fit <- coupled_diagonalization(   hd_multi,   ncomp = 5,   ncomp_per_domain = 12,   mu_coupling = 1.5,   knn = 8,   verbose = FALSE )  list(   converged = cd_fit$converged,   iterations = cd_fit$iterations,   final_cost = cd_fit$final_cost ) #> $converged #> [1] FALSE #>  #> $iterations #> [1] 200 #>  #> $final_cost #> [1] 0.04915779

title: Coupled Diagonalization across Modalities
text: inspect Frobenius norm coupled basis pairwise Hilbert-Schmidt similarities gauge alignment strength.
code: basis_norms <- purrr::imap_dfr(cd_fit$coupled_bases, function(Ai, name) {   tibble(domain = name, frobenius_norm = sqrt(sum(Ai^2))) })  basis_similarity <- function(A, B) sqrt(sum((t(A) %*% B)^2))  pair_indices <- combn(names(cd_fit$coupled_bases), 2, simplify = FALSE) similarity_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(pair_indices, function(pair) {   tibble(     domain_i = pair[1],     domain_j = pair[2],     hs_similarity = basis_similarity(cd_fit$coupled_bases[[pair[1]]],                                      cd_fit$coupled_bases[[pair[2]]])   ) })  basis_norms #> # A tibble: 3 × 2 #>   domain  frobenius_norm #>   <chr>            <dbl> #> 1 domain1           2.24 #> 2 domain2           2.24 #> 3 domain3           2.24 similarity_tbl #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   domain_i domain_j hs_similarity #>   <chr>    <chr>            <dbl> #> 1 domain1  domain2           2.08 #> 2 domain1  domain3           2.07 #> 3 domain2  domain3           2.01

code: rows <- list(   list(a = 1:10),   list(a = 11:20),   list(a = 21:30) )  fit_fn <- function(analysis) {   ids_a <- analysis$a$design$row_id   ids_b <- analysis$b$design$row_id    corr <- feature_correspondences(     features_true$a[ids_a, , drop = FALSE],     features_true$b[ids_b, , drop = FALSE]   )    manifoldalign::ssma_align(     analysis,     correspondences = corr,     preproc = multivarious::center(),     ncomp = 2,     control = manifoldalign::ssma_align_control(       knn = 8,       rank_per_domain = 12,       verbose = FALSE     )   ) }  cv_signal <- manifoldalign::cv_alignment_rows(   hd,   rows = rows,   fit_fn = fit_fn,   features = features_true,   k = 3,   target_pool = "analysis" )  cv_signal$scores #> # A tibble: 3 × 9 #>   mean_top1_similarity mean_topk_similarity oracle_top1_similarity #>                  <dbl>                <dbl>                  <dbl> #> 1                0.675                0.680                  0.999 #> 2                0.398                0.473                  1.000 #> 3                0.815                0.780                  1.000 #> # ℹ 6 more variables: oracle_topk_similarity <dbl>, top1_gap <dbl>, #> #   topk_gap <dbl>, n_queries <dbl>, n_pairs <dbl>, .fold <int>  stopifnot(all(is.finite(cv_signal$scores$mean_top1_similarity))) stopifnot(all(is.finite(cv_signal$scores$mean_topk_similarity))) stopifnot(mean(cv_signal$scores$mean_top1_similarity) > 0.5)

title: Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein for Domain Alignment
text: Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein (FPGW) distance powerful tool aligning domains : Different feature spaces (heterogeneous domains) Partial correspondence (samples need match) Combined attribute structural information vignette demonstrates use FPGW various domain alignment tasks.

title: Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein for Domain Alignment
text: simplest case aligns two domains using feature structural information:
code: # Create synthetic data with different dimensions set.seed(123) n1 <- 30 n2 <- 30  # Domain 1: 3D data X1 <- matrix(rnorm(n1 * 3), n1, 3) X1[1:15, ] <- X1[1:15, ] + 2  # Create two clusters  # Domain 2: 5D data with similar structure X2 <- matrix(rnorm(n2 * 5), n2, 5) X2[1:15, ] <- X2[1:15, ] + 2  # Create hyperdesign object design1 <- data.frame(id = 1:n1, cluster = rep(1:2, each = 15)) design2 <- data.frame(id = 1:n2, cluster = rep(1:2, each = 15))  md1 <- multidesign(X1, design1) md2 <- multidesign(X2, design2) hd <- hyperdesign(list(domain1 = md1, domain2 = md2))  # Compute FPGW alignment result <- fpgw(hd, omega1 = 0.5, verbose = TRUE) #> FPGW: Computing distance between domain 1 and 2 #>   Iteration  10: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration  20: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration  30: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration  40: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration  50: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration  60: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration  70: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration  80: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration  90: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 100: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 110: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 120: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 130: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 140: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 150: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 160: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 170: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 180: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 190: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 #>   Iteration 200: FW gap = 9.746e-01, alpha = 0.000 print(result) #> Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein #> ================================ #> Number of domains: 2  #> Domain names: domain1, domain2  #> Feature weight (omega1): 0.5  #> Mode: Classical Fused GW #>  #> Pairwise distances: #>        [,1]   [,2] #> [1,] 0.0000 0.4898 #> [2,] 0.4898 0.0000 #>  #> Warning: Some optimizations did not converge #> Non-converged pairs: #>   (domain1, domain2)

code: # Extract transport plan P <- result$transport_plans[[1]]  # Find strongest connections threshold <- 0.05 strong_connections <- which(P > threshold, arr.ind = TRUE) head(strong_connections) #>      row col  # Visualize transport plan image(P, main = "FPGW Transport Plan",        xlab = "Domain 1", ylab = "Domain 2",       col = heat.colors(100))

title: Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein for Domain Alignment
text: domains outliers noise, may want transport fraction mass:
code: # Add outliers to domain 2 X2_noisy <- rbind(X2, matrix(rnorm(10 * 5, sd = 5), 10, 5)) design2_noisy <- data.frame(id = 1:(n2 + 10),                             cluster = c(rep(1:2, each = 15), rep(3, 10)))  md2_noisy <- multidesign(X2_noisy, design2_noisy) hd_noisy <- hyperdesign(list(domain1 = md1, domain2 = md2_noisy))  # Transport only 80% of mass to avoid outliers result_partial <- fpgw(hd_noisy, omega1 = 0.5, rho = 0.8)  # Check transported mass P_partial <- result_partial$transport_plans[[1]] cat("Total transported mass:", sum(P_partial), "\n") #> Total transported mass: 0.2564186

title: Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein for Domain Alignment
text: total variation penalty provides soft constraint transported mass:
code: # Use TV penalty instead of hard mass constraint result_tv <- fpgw(hd_noisy, omega1 = 0.5, lambda = 0.1)  P_tv <- result_tv$transport_plans[[1]] cat("Total transported mass with TV penalty:", sum(P_tv), "\n") #> Total transported mass with TV penalty: 0.2564186

") #> Structural emphasis distance: 0.2036896 cat("Balanced distance:", result_balanced$distances[1,2], "
") #> Balanced distance: 0.4897807 cat("Feature emphasis distance:", result_feature$distances[1,2], "

title: Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein for Domain Alignment
text: FPGW can align multiple domains simultaneously:
code: # Create three domains with varying dimensions X3 <- matrix(rnorm(25 * 4), 25, 4) X3[1:12, ] <- X3[1:12, ] + 2  design3 <- data.frame(id = 1:25, cluster = c(rep(1, 12), rep(2, 13))) md3 <- multidesign(X3, design3)  # Create hyperdesign with three domains hd_multi <- hyperdesign(list(   domain1 = md1,   domain2 = md2,   domain3 = md3 ))  # Compute pairwise alignments result_multi <- fpgw(hd_multi, omega1 = 0.3)  # Distance matrix between all domains print(result_multi$distances) #>           [,1]      [,2]      [,3] #> [1,] 0.0000000 0.6346543 0.6482231 #> [2,] 0.6346543 0.0000000 0.6902467 #> [3,] 0.6482231 0.6902467 0.0000000

title: Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein for Domain Alignment
text: FPGW implementation uses optimized C++ code performance:
code: # Compare performance for different problem sizes sizes <- c(20, 50, 100) times <- numeric(length(sizes))  for (i in seq_along(sizes)) {   n <- sizes[i]   X1_test <- matrix(rnorm(n * 5), n, 5)   X2_test <- matrix(rnorm(n * 5), n, 5)      design_test <- data.frame(id = 1:n)   hd_test <- hyperdesign(list(     d1 = multidesign(X1_test, design_test),     d2 = multidesign(X2_test, design_test)   ))      times[i] <- system.time({     fpgw(hd_test, omega1 = 0.5, max_iter = 10, verbose = FALSE)   })[3] }  plot(sizes, times, type = "b",       xlab = "Problem size (n)", ylab = "Time (seconds)",      main = "FPGW Scaling Performance")

title: Generalized PCA Alignment with gpca_align
text: reuse packaged benchmark dataset every alignment vignette operates identical inputs. contains three domains two latent classes moderate domain-specific transformations. data hyperdesign, call gpca_align() supply label column name via y argument. result multiblock_biprojector, can extract scores feature loadings just like multivarious models. plotting z-score aligned scores scale matches vignettes. can optionally pass domain-specific preprocessing list (e.g. list(center(), center(), center())) want centre scale block alignment. Passing base_preproc list (built multivarious::pass()) keeps preprocessing identity—keeps example lightweight still supporting different feature dimensions.

attr(*, "class")= chr [1:5] "gpca_align" "multiblock_biprojector" "multiblock_projector" "bi_projector" ... #>  - attr(*, ".cache")=<environment: 0x55a4f6354248> rms_alignment(as.matrix(gpca_fit$s), domain_sizes, domain_names) #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   domain_i domain_j    rms #>   <chr>    <chr>     <dbl> #> 1 domain1  domain2  0.205  #> 2 domain1  domain3  0.231  #> 3 domain2  domain3  0.0333 score_tbl <- as_tibble(zscore_columns(as.matrix(gpca_fit$s)), .name_repair = "minimal") colnames(score_tbl) <- paste0("comp", seq_len(ncol(score_tbl)))  scores <- score_tbl %>%   mutate(     sample = seq_len(nrow(.)),     domain = rep(domain_names, times = domain_sizes),     condition = rep(labels, length(domain_names))   )  head(scores) #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>    comp1 comp2 sample domain  condition #>    <dbl> <dbl>  <int> <chr>   <fct>     #> 1 -0.819 0.674      1 domain1 class_A   #> 2 -1.48  1.38       2 domain1 class_A   #> 3 -1.18  1.11       3 domain1 class_A   #> 4 -1.95  1.96       4 domain1 class_A   #> 5 -1.08  0.997      5 domain1 class_A   #> 6 -1.45  1.33       6 domain1 class_A

title: Spectral Graph Alignment with grasp
code: library(manifoldalign) library(multidesign) library(multivarious) library(tibble) library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(scales)

title: Spectral Graph Alignment with grasp
code: alignment_benchmark <- manifoldalign::alignment_benchmark pair_domains <- alignment_benchmark$domains[1:2]  pair_multidesign <- lapply(pair_domains, function(dom) {   multidesign::multidesign(dom$x, dom$design) })  pair_names <- names(pair_multidesign) node_counts <- vapply(pair_multidesign, function(dom) nrow(dom$x), integer(1))  hd_pair <- multidesign::hyperdesign(pair_multidesign)

title: Spectral Graph Alignment with grasp
code: grasp_internal <- grasp(   hd_pair,   ncomp = 20,   q_descriptors = 80,   sigma = 0.8,   lambda = 0.1,   solver = "linear" )  str(grasp_internal$assignment) #>  int [1:80] 79 66 29 53 37 13 7 61 17 65 ...

title: Spectral Graph Alignment with grasp
text: assignment component maps nodes second domain nodes first (reference) domain. compare assigned pairs underlying class labels quantify alignment quality—remember optimiser never sees labels.
code: assignment <- grasp_internal$assignment ref_design <- pair_multidesign[[1]]$design cmp_design <- pair_multidesign[[2]]$design  class_accuracy <- mean(ref_design$condition == cmp_design$condition[assignment]) identity_fraction <- mean(assignment == seq_along(assignment))  tibble(   metric = c("Class agreement", "Exact identity"),   value = c(class_accuracy, identity_fraction) ) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   metric           value #>   <chr>            <dbl> #> 1 Class agreement 0.475  #> 2 Exact identity  0.0125 n_ref <- node_counts[1] embed1 <- grasp_internal$s[seq_len(n_ref), , drop = FALSE] embed2 <- grasp_internal$s[n_ref + seq_len(n_ref), , drop = FALSE] final_err <- sqrt(mean(rowSums((embed1 - embed2)^2)))  tibble(   metric = "Post-alignment RMS error",   value = final_err ) #> # A tibble: 1 × 2 #>   metric                   value #>   <chr>                    <dbl> #> 1 Post-alignment RMS error  1.28

title: Spectral Graph Alignment with grasp
text: stack aligned embeddings domains (returned grasp()) colour points latent class.
code: embed1 <- grasp_internal$s[seq_len(n_ref), , drop = FALSE] embed2 <- grasp_internal$s[n_ref + seq_len(n_ref), , drop = FALSE]  score_tbl <- as_tibble(rbind(embed1, embed2), .name_repair = "minimal") colnames(score_tbl) <- paste0("comp", seq_len(ncol(score_tbl)))  scores <- score_tbl %>%   mutate(     sample = seq_len(nrow(.)),     domain = rep(pair_names, each = nrow(embed1)),     condition = c(ref_design$condition, cmp_design$condition[assignment])   )   ggplot(scores, aes(x = comp1, y = comp2, colour = condition, shape = domain)) +   geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.85) +   labs(title = "GRASP alignment: first two components",        x = "Component 1", y = "Component 2") +   theme_minimal()

title: Kernel Manifold Alignment with kema
text: exact solver tackles generalized eigenvalue problem directly. faithful slower large kernels. quick sanity check compares subspaces recovered two solvers.
code: exact_fit <- kema(   hd,   y = condition,   ncomp = 2,   knn = 3,   sigma = 0.8,   solver = "exact",   preproc = multivarious::pass() )  exact_fit$eigenvalues$values #> [1] 0.01373906 0.49999987 rms_alignment(as.matrix(exact_fit$s), domain_sizes, domain_names) #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   domain_i domain_j     rms #>   <chr>    <chr>      <dbl> #> 1 domain1  domain2  0.0130  #> 2 domain1  domain3  0.0119  #> 3 domain2  domain3  0.00116 subspace_similarity <- function(A, B) {   A <- as.matrix(A)   B <- as.matrix(B)   Qa <- qr.Q(qr(A))   Qb <- qr.Q(qr(B))   svd(t(Qa) %*% Qb, nu = 0, nv = 0)$d }  subspace_similarity(reg_fit$s[, 1:2], exact_fit$s[, 1:2]) #> [1] 1 1

code: rekema_fit <- kema(   hd,   y = condition,   ncomp = 2,   knn = 3,   sigma = 0.8,   solver = "exact",   sample_frac = 0.5,   preproc = multivarious::pass() )  rekema_fit$eigenvalues$solver #> [1] "exact" rms_alignment(as.matrix(rekema_fit$s), domain_sizes, domain_names) #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   domain_i domain_j     rms #>   <chr>    <chr>      <dbl> #> 1 domain1  domain2  0.00696 #> 2 domain1  domain3  0.00890 #> 3 domain2  domain3  0.0117 subspace_similarity(exact_fit$s[, 1:2], rekema_fit$s[, 1:2]) #> [1] 0.86740310 0.04146403

title: Kernel Manifold Alignment with kema
text: Enabling kema.scalable_mode activates low-rank label-factor matrix-free kernel path introduced accompanying refactor. keeps API identical avoiding dense n \times n intermediates. scalable path agree closely baseline exact solution.
code: old_opts <- options(kema.scalable_mode = TRUE) on.exit(options(old_opts), add = TRUE)  scalable_fit <- kema(   hd,   y = condition,   ncomp = 2,   knn = 3,   sigma = 0.8,   solver = "exact",   preproc = multivarious::pass() )  scalable_fit$eigenvalues$solver #> [1] "exact" rms_alignment(as.matrix(scalable_fit$s), domain_sizes, domain_names) #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   domain_i domain_j     rms #>   <chr>    <chr>      <dbl> #> 1 domain1  domain2  0.0130  #> 2 domain1  domain3  0.0119  #> 3 domain2  domain3  0.00116 subspace_similarity(exact_fit$s[, 1:2], scalable_fit$s[, 1:2]) #> [1] 1 1

title: Kernel Manifold Alignment with kema
text: graph neighbourhood size knn, Gaussian kernel width sigma, trade-u immediate levers practice. Smaller sigma emphasises local structure, larger u leans label agreement. grid reports mean RMS alignment (smaller better) representative settings. embedding geometry shifts noticeably configurations lowest highest mean RMS:  general, tighter kernels (sigma = 0.5) modest neighbourhoods (knn = 3) balanced supervision (u = 0.5) yield consistent alignment benchmark, overly wide kernels heavy supervision degrade overlap. Use diagnostics template tuning larger data.
code: parameter_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(   sigma = c(0.5, 0.8, 1.1),   knn = c(3, 6),   u = c(0.35, 0.5, 0.7) )  grid_summary <- parameter_grid %>%   mutate(     mean_rms = purrr::pmap_dbl(       list(sigma, knn, u),       function(sigma, knn, u) {         fit <- kema(           hd,           y = condition,           ncomp = 2,           knn = knn,           sigma = sigma,           u = u,           solver = "regression",           preproc = multivarious::pass()         )          mean(rms_alignment(as.matrix(fit$s), domain_sizes, domain_names)$rms)       }     )   ) %>%   arrange(mean_rms)  grid_summary #> # A tibble: 18 × 4 #>    sigma   knn     u mean_rms #>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl> #>  1   0.5     3  0.5  0.000172 #>  2   0.5     6  0.5  0.000198 #>  3   0.8     3  0.7  0.00866  #>  4   0.8     6  0.7  0.00867  #>  5   0.8     3  0.35 0.00867  #>  6   0.8     6  0.35 0.00868  #>  7   0.8     6  0.5  0.00868  #>  8   0.8     3  0.5  0.00869  #>  9   0.5     3  0.7  0.00937  #> 10   0.5     3  0.35 0.00950  #> 11   0.5     6  0.7  0.00952  #> 12   0.5     6  0.35 0.00955  #> 13   1.1     3  0.7  0.00961  #> 14   1.1     6  0.7  0.00961  #> 15   1.1     3  0.5  0.00962  #> 16   1.1     6  0.5  0.00962  #> 17   1.1     3  0.35 0.00962  #> 18   1.1     6  0.35 0.00962 best_cfg <- grid_summary %>% slice_min(mean_rms, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) worst_cfg <- grid_summary %>% slice_max(mean_rms, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)  collect_scores <- function(cfg, tag) {   fit <- kema(     hd,     y = condition,     ncomp = 2,     knn = cfg$knn[[1]],     sigma = cfg$sigma[[1]],     u = cfg$u[[1]],     solver = "regression",     preproc = multivarious::pass()   )    tbl <- as_tibble(zscore_columns(as.matrix(fit$s)), .name_repair = "minimal")   colnames(tbl) <- paste0("comp", seq_len(ncol(tbl)))    tbl %>%     mutate(       domain = rep(domain_names, times = domain_sizes),       condition = replicated_labels,       config = tag     ) }  comparison_scores <- dplyr::bind_rows(   collect_scores(best_cfg, "low mean RMS"),   collect_scores(worst_cfg, "high mean RMS") )   ggplot(comparison_scores, aes(x = comp1, y = comp2, colour = condition, shape = domain)) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.85, size = 2.1) +   facet_wrap(~ config) +   labs(     title = "Effect of kernel and graph parameters",     x = "Component 1",     y = "Component 2"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: Low-Rank Alignment with lowrank_align
text: start packaged alignment_benchmark dataset, convert domain multidesign objects, deliberately mask subset labels illustrate semi-supervised behaviour.
code: alignment_benchmark <- manifoldalign::alignment_benchmark  # Convert each domain to a multidesign object domain_list <- lapply(alignment_benchmark$domains, function(dom) {   multidesign(dom$x, dom$design) })  domain_names <- names(domain_list) domain_sizes <- vapply(domain_list, function(dom) nrow(dom$x), integer(1))  # Hide labels in alternating batches for the first two domains semi_domain_list <- domain_list semi_domain_list[[1]]$design$condition[seq(1, domain_sizes[1], by = 4)] <- NA semi_domain_list[[2]]$design$condition[seq(2, domain_sizes[2], by = 4)] <- NA  semi_hd <- hyperdesign(semi_domain_list) observed_labels <- purrr::map(semi_domain_list, ~ .x$design$condition) %>% unlist()  label_status <- tibble(   domain = rep(domain_names, times = domain_sizes),   status = if_else(is.na(observed_labels), "unlabeled", "labeled") ) %>%   count(domain, status)  label_status #> # A tibble: 5 × 3 #>   domain  status        n #>   <chr>   <chr>     <int> #> 1 domain1 labeled      60 #> 2 domain1 unlabeled    20 #> 3 domain2 labeled      60 #> 4 domain2 unlabeled    20 #> 5 domain3 labeled      80

what: Similarity Function for the Laplacian Term
title: Low-Rank Alignment with lowrank_align
text: lowrank_align expects simfun turns (possibly NA) label vector affinity matrix. helper links samples share observed label leaves unlabeled rows/columns zero, dovetails Laplacian masking performed inside lowrank_align().
code: label_similarity <- function(labels) {   labs <- as.character(labels)   valid_levels <- unique(labs[!is.na(labs)])   n <- length(labs)   sim <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = n)    for (lvl in valid_levels) {     idx <- which(labs == lvl)     if (length(idx) > 1) {       sim[idx, idx] <- 1     }   }    diag(sim) <- 0   sim }  # Quick sanity check on a small slice label_similarity(observed_labels[1:6]) #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] #> [1,]    0    0    0    0    0    0 #> [2,]    0    0    1    1    0    1 #> [3,]    0    1    0    1    0    1 #> [4,]    0    1    1    0    0    1 #> [5,]    0    0    0    0    0    0 #> [6,]    0    1    1    1    0    0

code: alignment_benchmark <- manifoldalign::alignment_benchmark pair_domains <- alignment_benchmark$domains[1:2]  # Convert to multidesign objects pair_multidesign <- lapply(pair_domains, function(dom) {   multidesign::multidesign(dom$x, dom$design) })  # Add matching anchors (10 nodes) to each domain's design frame set.seed(123) num_anchors <- 10 anchor_idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(pair_multidesign[[1]]$x)), num_anchors)  pair_multidesign[[1]]$design$anchor_id <- NA_integer_ pair_multidesign[[1]]$design$anchor_id[anchor_idx] <- anchor_idx pair_multidesign[[2]]$design$anchor_id <- NA_integer_ pair_multidesign[[2]]$design$anchor_id[anchor_idx] <- anchor_idx  pair_names <- names(pair_multidesign) node_counts <- vapply(pair_multidesign, function(dom) nrow(dom$x), integer(1))  hd_pair <- multidesign::hyperdesign(pair_multidesign)

title: Alignment Method Performance Overview

Supervision level: anchors partial labels available, algorithms incorporate (KEMA, PARROT, pseudolabel) typically outperform purely unsupervised methods. title: Manifold Alignment for Multi-Domain Data
code: library(manifoldalign)  # Create two domains with shared structure set.seed(1) X1 <- matrix(rnorm(100 * 20), 100, 20) X2 <- matrix(rnorm(80 * 15), 80, 15) labels1 <- rep(1:4, each = 25) labels2 <- rep(1:4, each = 20)  # Build a hyperdesign (multi-domain container) hd <- as_hyperdesign(   list(X1, X2),   labels = list(labels1, labels2) )  # Align with KEMA result <- kema(hd, ncomp = 5)  # Or align with Generalized Procrustes result <- generalized_procrustes(hd, ncomp = 5)

code: assign_pseudolabels(   sim_matrix,   min_clusters = 10,   max_clusters = 100,   sim_threshold = NULL,   min_cluster_size = 2,   max_cluster_size = Inf,   diversity_weight = 0.3,   adaptive_threshold_quantile = 0.8,   seed = NULL,   use_advanced_diversity = TRUE,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Assign pseudolabels based on sparse similarity matrix clustering — assign_pseudolabels
text: sim_matrix Sparse similarity matrix (dgCMatrix similar). symmetric values 0 1, higher values indicate greater similarity. min_clusters Minimum number clusters find (default: 10) max_clusters Maximum number clusters find (default: 100) sim_threshold Minimum similarity threshold cluster membership. NULL, adaptively determined distribution non-zero similarities. min_cluster_size Minimum number samples required form cluster (default: 2) max_cluster_size Maximum number samples allowed cluster (default: Inf) diversity_weight Weight promoting diversity among cluster representatives [0,1]. Controls trade-diversity cluster confidence: 0 = select largest/confident clusters, 1 = maximize diversity (minimize pairwise similarities), 0.5 = balanced approach (default: 0.3) adaptive_threshold_quantile Quantile non-zero similarities use adaptive threshold (default: 0.8) seed Random seed reproducibility use_advanced_diversity Whether use advanced farthest-first traversal diversity selection large candidate sets (default: TRUE) verbose Whether print progress information (default: FALSE)

title: Assign pseudolabels based on sparse similarity matrix clustering — assign_pseudolabels
text: list containing: labels Factor vector pseudolabels, NA unassigned     samples representatives Integer vector row indices serving cluster     representatives cluster_info Data frame cluster statistics including cluster     ID, representative index, size, average similarity threshold_used similarity threshold applied n_clusters Number clusters found

title: Assign pseudolabels based on sparse similarity matrix clustering — assign_pseudolabels
text: algorithm works several steps: Determine similarity threshold (adaptive user-specified) Build graph high-similarity connections Find connected components initial clusters Select diverse representatives clusters Optionally merge small clusters split large ones diversity constraint helps ensure cluster representatives spread across similarity space, making better anchors domain alignment.

title: Assign pseudolabels based on sparse similarity matrix clustering — assign_pseudolabels
code: # \donttest{ # Create example sparse similarity matrix library(Matrix) n <- 1000 # Generate random sparse matrix with values in [0,1] sim_matrix <- Matrix::rsparsematrix(n, n, density = 0.05, rand.x = runif) sim_matrix <- (sim_matrix + Matrix::t(sim_matrix)) / 2  # Make symmetric Matrix::diag(sim_matrix) <- 1  # Self-similarity = 1  # Find pseudolabels result <- assign_pseudolabels(sim_matrix, min_clusters = 20, verbose = TRUE) #> Processing 1000 samples with 97248 non-zero similarities #> Adaptive threshold: 0.4069 ( 0.8 quantile of 97248 similarities) #> After thresholding: 19450 connections remain #> Found 1 initial clusters #> Found 1 valid clusters after size filtering #> Warning: Final number of representatives (1) is below min_clusters (20). Consider lowering sim_threshold or min_cluster_size. #> Final result: 1 clusters, 1000 samples assigned table(result$labels, useNA = "always") #>  #> anchor_001       <NA>  #>       1000          0  # }

text: sizes Integer vector node counts benchmark. d Integer feature dimension synthetic node features. noise_sd Numeric noise standard deviation added target features. structure Synthetic geometry base node coordinates: `"ring"`, `"grid"`, `"random"`, `"community"`. permute_fraction Fraction nodes permute (`(0,1]`). n_anchors Integer number anchor correspondences add (0 allowed). methods Character vector methods run. Options include: `"token_ot_graph"`, `"cone_align"`, `"grasp"`, `"parrot"`, `"fpgw"`, `"ssma"`, `"lra"`, `"gpca"`. decode_mode Decoding mode mapping source nodes targets: `"native"` uses method's native assignment/transport decoding; `"common_nn"` uses nearest-neighbor decoding aligned scores methods; `"common_procrustes_lap"` uses anchor-Procrustes (anchors available) followed LAP/Hungarian decoding aligned scores. ssma_procrustes Logical; `FALSE` (default), SSMA ignores `"common_procrustes_lap"` decodes common space via nearest-neighbor (`"common_nn"`). Set `TRUE` explicitly benchmark `SSMA+Procrustes` decode variant. candidate_k Integer number candidates per source node `token_ot_graph_align()`. coarsen_method Coarsening method multilevel Token-OT alignment: `"kmeans"` `"louvain"`. token_mode Tokenization mode passed [token_ot_graph_align_control()]. views Views passed [token_ot_graph_align_control()]. n_levels Integer number multilevel hierarchy levels `token_ot_graph_align()`. prior_mode Prior lifting mode multilevel (`"none"`, `"hard"`, `"soft"`). fpgw_omega1 Weight feature term `fpgw()` (0–1). fpgw_epsilon Entropic warm-start regularization `fpgw()`. fpgw_max_iter Maximum Frank-Wolfe iterations `fpgw()`. fpgw_inner_max_iter Inner iterations `fpgw()` updates. fpgw_tol Convergence tolerance `fpgw()`. ssma_solver Solver passed [ssma_align_control()] `ssma_align()`. ssma_knn Integer k within-domain graph construction SSMA. ssma_rank_per_domain Integer per-domain rank cap SSMA reduction. ssma_use_serial Logical; `TRUE`, enable serial decontamination SSMA. ssma_lag_exclusion Non-negative lag exclusion radius SSMA serial hard masking `ssma_use_serial = TRUE`. lra_mu Mixing parameter `lowrank_align()` (`mu` argument). lra_lambda Ridge parameter passed `lowrank_align()`. lra_sv_thresh Singular-value threshold passed `lowrank_align()`. lra_solver Solver backend passed `lowrank_align()`. gpca_u Within/trade-parameter passed `gpca_align()`. gpca_lambda Ridge regularization passed `gpca_align()`. n_reps Integer number replications per size. seed Integer seed reproducibility. verbose Logical; print per-run progress.

title: CONE-Align: Consensus Optimization for Node Embedding Alignment — cone_align
text: CONE-Align tackles graph alignment iteratively refining orthogonal transformations node--node correspondences. algorithm alternates two steps: (1) finding optimal orthogonal rotations given current assignments via Procrustes analysis, (2) updating assignments given current transformations via linear assignment. CONE-Align operates following algorithmic blocks: Spectral Embedding: Compute Laplacian eigenmaps graph Orthogonal Alignment: Find rotation matrices via Procrustes analysis Assignment Update: Solve linear assignment problem correspondences Convergence Check: Iterate assignments stabilize algorithm minimizes objective: $$\sum_{,j} ||Q_i^T Z_i - P_{ij} Q_j^T Z_j||_F^2$$ \(Z_i\) embeddings, \(Q_i\) orthogonal transforms, \(P_{ij}\) permutation matrices. Key parameters: ncomp: Dimension spectral embeddings sigma: Bandwidth embedding computation lambda: Regularization numerical stability solver: Assignment algorithm ("linear" "auction") CONE-Align tackles graph alignment iteratively refining orthogonal transformations node--node correspondences. algorithm alternates two steps: (1) finding optimal orthogonal rotations given current assignments via Procrustes analysis, (2) updating assignments given current transformations via linear assignment. CONE-Align operates following algorithmic blocks: Spectral Embedding: Compute Laplacian eigenmaps graph Orthogonal Alignment: Find rotation matrices via     Procrustes analysis Assignment Update: Solve linear assignment problem     correspondences Convergence Check: Iterate assignments stabilize algorithm minimizes objective: $$\sum_{,j} ||Q_i^T Z_i - P_{ij} Q_j^T Z_j||_F^2$$ \(Z_i\) embeddings, \(Q_i\) orthogonal transforms, \(P_{ij}\) permutation matrices. Currently supports *exactly two* domains. multi-graph alignment three domains, see cone_align_multiple. Key parameters: ncomp: Dimension spectral embeddings sigma: Bandwidth embedding computation lambda: Regularization numerical stability solver: Assignment algorithm ("linear" "auction") knn: Number nearest neighbors graph construction

title: Coupled Diagonalization for Multi-Modal Alignment — coupled_diagonalization
text: Coupled Diagonalization (Eynard et al. 2015) extends spectral methods multi-modal data finding bases simultaneously diagonalize individual Laplacians aligned correspondence constraints. algorithm uses Stiefel manifold optimization maintain orthogonality constraints. algorithm minimizes objective function: $$F() = sum_i ||A_i^T L_i A_i - diag(A_i^T L_i A_i)||_F^2 + mu_c sum_{<j} ||F_i^T U_i A_i - F_j^T U_j A_j||_F^2$$ : A_i coupling matrices Stiefel manifold L_i eigenvalues -th Laplacian U_i eigenvectors -th Laplacian F_i correspondence matrices modalities mu_c controls coupling strength first term encourages diagonalization individual Laplacians, second term enforces alignment correspondences. algorithm uses projected gradient descent Stiefel manifold maintain orthogonality. Key features: Handles partial correspondences modalities Preserves manifold structure graph Laplacians Maintains orthogonality via Stiefel manifold optimization Supports semi-supervised learning missing correspondences algorithm minimizes objective uses projected gradient descent Stiefel manifold maintain orthogonality coupling matrices A_i. alpha_match > 0, optional match term nudges diagonal entries A_i^T Lambda_i A_i toward user-specified target eigenvalues (without adding extra -diagonal penalty).
code: F = sum_i ||A_i^T Lambda_i A_i - diag(A_i^T Lambda_i A_i)||_F^2 +     mu_c sum_{i<j} ||F_i^T U_i A_i - F_j^T U_j A_j||_F^2

code: # \donttest{ # Example with hyperdesign data library(multidesign)  # Create synthetic multi-modal data set.seed(123) # Domain 1: 3D data X1 <- matrix(rnorm(150), 50, 3) # Domain 2: 4D data   X2 <- matrix(rnorm(200), 50, 4)  # Create design with full correspondence design1 <- data.frame(sample_id = 1:50) design2 <- data.frame(sample_id = 1:50)  # Create multidesign objects md1 <- multidesign(X1, design1) md2 <- multidesign(X2, design2)  # Create hyperdesign hd <- hyperdesign(list(domain1 = md1, domain2 = md2))  # Run coupled diagonalization with default settings result <- coupled_diagonalization(hd, ncomp = 3) #> sigma is 1.53794640409146 #> sigma is 1.85511070143682  # Access coupled bases coupled_scores <- result$s coupled_bases <- result$coupled_bases  # With partial correspondences # Specify correspondence matrix (e.g., only first 30 samples correspond) F_partial <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(i = 1:30, j = 1:30, x = 1, dims = c(50, 50)) result_partial <- coupled_diagonalization(hd,                                          correspondence = list(F_partial, F_partial),                                         ncomp = 3) #> sigma is 1.53794640409146 #> sigma is 1.85511070143682 # }  # \donttest{ library(multidesign) # Create synthetic multi-modal data X1 <- matrix(rnorm(150), 50, 3) X2 <- matrix(rnorm(200), 50, 4)  # Create hyperdesign hd <- hyperdesign(list(   domain1 = multidesign(X1, data.frame(id = 1:50)),   domain2 = multidesign(X2, data.frame(id = 1:50)) ))  # Run coupled diagonalization result <- coupled_diagonalization(hd, ncomp = 3) #> sigma is 1.48550141814904 #> sigma is 1.96203797806432 # }

code: .generalized_procrustes_impl(   A_list,   task_labels_list,   L,   max_iter = 100,   tol = 1e-06,   tol_type = c("relative", "absolute"),   verbose = FALSE,   svd_method = c("irlba", "base"),   svd_opts = list() )

title: Generalized Orthogonal Procrustes with Partial Tasks — .generalized_procrustes_impl
text: A_list list length \(n\), element \(A_i\) \(d x li\) numeric matrix representing observed data subject \(\). subject might different \(li < L\). task_labels_list list length \(n\), \(task_labels_list[[]]\) integer (numeric) vector length \(li\), specifying global tasks column \(A_i\) corresponds (\(1..L\)). L Integer. total number distinct tasks across subjects. max_iter Integer. Maximum number GPM iterations. Default 100. tol Numeric tolerance convergence. Default 1e-6. tol_type Character. Type tolerance ("relative" "absolute"). Note: relative tolerance calculated `sqrt(diff_sq) / norm0`, `norm0` Frobenius norm initial `O_mats` (plus epsilon stability). absolute tolerance uses `sqrt(diff_sq) / (sqrt(n*d) + 1)`. Default "relative". verbose Logical. TRUE, prints iteration info. Default FALSE. svd_method Backend initial SVD (one "irlba", "base"). "irlba" recommended used default, fallback random initialization needed. "base" forces use dense SVD, can slow/memory-intensive. Default "irlba". svd_opts List extra arguments passed irlba::irlba base::svd.

title: Generalized Orthogonal Procrustes with Partial Tasks — .generalized_procrustes_impl
text: list : O_mats List \(n\) orthogonal \(d \times d\) matrices. A_est \(d \times L\) consensus matrix. Columns corresponding   tasks observed subjects contain NA. iterations Number iterations performed. converged Logical indicating whether GPM converged. final_diff final difference value (`sqrt(diff_sq)`) used   convergence check.

title: Generalized Orthogonal Procrustes with Partial Tasks — .generalized_procrustes_impl
text: Sparse Construction D: form large sparse matrix \(D \R^{(n d) \times L}\) using Matrix::sparseMatrix. Triplet indices (row, column, value) collected efficiently. Robust Initialization: Initialization uses top \(d\) left singular vectors \(D\), typically computed via irlba::irlba. irlba fails returns rank deficient result (less \(d\) vectors), falls back initializing random orthogonal matrices ensure robustness. Vectorized GPM Iteration: core iteration avoids \(O(n^2)\) complexity computing update term \(CO\) using two efficient sparse matrix multiplications: \(Y <- D^T * stack(O_{old})\) \(CO_{stack} <- D * Y\) \(stack(O)\) reshapes \(d \times d \times n\) array rotation matrices \((nd) \times d\) matrix. resulting \((nd) \times d\) matrix \(CO_{stack}\) unstacked back \(d \times d \times n\) array. Efficient Projection: \(d \times d\) slice unstacked update projected onto orthogonal group O(d). efficient projection method (.projO) used, switching eigenvalue-based method small \(d\) SVD-based method larger \(d\). Convergence Check: Convergence assessed comparing Frobenius norm difference consecutive projected iterates \(O_{new}\) \(O_{old}\). relative tolerance, difference scaled Frobenius norm initial \(O\) matrices (calculated ). Final Consensus A_est: convergence, consensus matrix \(A_{est}\) computed. task \(j\), average transformed data \(O_i^T A_i(*, j_i)\) subjects \(\) \(S_j\) observed task \(j\). Task counts (number subjects observing task \(j\)) computed directly iterating task_labels_list, ensuring correctness even input matrices contain explicit zeros.

title: Generalized Orthogonal Procrustes with Partial Tasks — .generalized_procrustes_impl
code: # \donttest{ # Simple example with 2 subjects and 3 tasks A1 <- matrix(rnorm(12), 3, 4)  # Subject 1: 3 features x 4 tasks A2 <- matrix(rnorm(9), 3, 3)   # Subject 2: 3 features x 3 tasks  # Task labels (partial overlap) task_labels1 <- c(1, 2, 3, 4)  # Subject 1 observes tasks 1,2,3,4 task_labels2 <- c(1, 3, 5)     # Subject 2 observes tasks 1,3,5  # Run alignment result <- generalized_procrustes(   A_list = list(A1, A2),   task_labels_list = list(task_labels1, task_labels2),   L = 5,  # Total of 5 unique tasks   max_iter = 50,   verbose = FALSE )  # Check results print(result$converged) #> [1] FALSE print(dim(result$A_est))  # Should be 3x5 #> [1] 3 5 # }

title: Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein Distance — fpgw
text: FPGW distance combines feature structural information : $$L(\gamma) = \omega_1 \langle C, \gamma \rangle +       \omega_2 \sum_{,j,',j'} |C_{X,ii'} - C_{Y,jj'}|^2 \gamma_{ij} \gamma_{'j'} +       \lambda(|\mu|^2 + |\nu|^2 - 2|\gamma|^2)$$ C feature cost matrix C_X, C_Y within-domain distance matrices. algorithm supports two variants: Mass-constrained: Transports exactly rho mass domains Penalized: Uses TV regularization parameter lambda Frank-Wolfe algorithm used closed-form step sizes efficiency.

title: Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein Distance — fpgw
code: # \donttest{ library(multidesign)  # Example 1: Basic FPGW between two domains with different dimensions set.seed(123) n <- 30  # Domain 1: 3D data with two clusters X1 <- matrix(rnorm(n * 3), n, 3) X1[1:15, ] <- X1[1:15, ] + 2  # Domain 2: 5D data with similar structure X2 <- matrix(rnorm(n * 5), n, 5) X2[1:15, ] <- X2[1:15, ] + 2  # Create hyperdesign design <- data.frame(id = 1:n, cluster = rep(1:2, each = 15)) hd <- hyperdesign(list(   visual = multidesign(X1, design),   semantic = multidesign(X2, design) ))  # Classical FGW with balanced feature/structure weight result <- fpgw(hd, omega1 = 0.5) print(result) #> Fused-Partial Gromov-Wasserstein #> ================================ #> Number of domains: 2  #> Domain names: visual, semantic  #> Feature weight (omega1): 0.5  #> Mode: Classical Fused GW #>  #> Pairwise distances: #>        [,1]   [,2] #> [1,] 0.0000 0.4898 #> [2,] 0.4898 0.0000 #>  #> Warning: Some optimizations did not converge #> Non-converged pairs: #>   (visual, semantic)  # Example 2: Mass-constrained for noisy data # Add outliers to domain 2 X2_noisy <- rbind(X2, matrix(rnorm(10 * 5, sd = 5), 10, 5)) design_noisy <- data.frame(id = 1:(n + 10))  hd_noisy <- hyperdesign(list(   clean = multidesign(X1, design[1:n,]),   noisy = multidesign(X2_noisy, design_noisy) ))  # Transport only 75% of mass to avoid outliers result_partial <- fpgw(hd_noisy, omega1 = 0.3, rho = 0.75)  # Check transported mass P <- result_partial$transport_plans[[1]] cat("Transported mass:", sum(P), "\n") #> Transported mass: 0.5528314   # Example 3: Multi-domain alignment X3 <- matrix(rnorm(n * 4), n, 4) X3[16:30, ] <- X3[16:30, ] + 1.5  hd_multi <- hyperdesign(list(   modality1 = multidesign(X1, design),   modality2 = multidesign(X2, design),   modality3 = multidesign(X3, design) ))  # Compute all pairwise alignments result_multi <- fpgw(hd_multi, omega1 = 0.2, max_iter = 50)  # Examine distance matrix print(result_multi$distances) #>           [,1]      [,2]      [,3] #> [1,] 0.0000000 0.6979227 0.5977135 #> [2,] 0.6979227 0.0000000 0.6298517 #> [3,] 0.5977135 0.6298517 0.0000000 # title: Generalized Orthogonal Procrustes Alignment — generalized_procrustes
text: method extends classical Procrustes analysis handle partial task observations, domain may observe subset global set tasks. algorithm uses efficient Generalized Power Method (GPM) sparse matrix operations robust initialization find optimal orthogonal transformations. Generalized Procrustes problem seeks find orthogonal matrices \(O_i\) domain \(\) minimize: $$\sum_{,j} \sum_{k \T_{ij}} ||O_i^T A_i(:,k) - O_j^T A_j(:,k)||^2$$ \(T_{ij}\) represents set tasks observed domains \(\) \(j\). algorithm handles several key challenges: Partial observations: domain may observe different     subsets tasks Sparse structure: Uses efficient sparse matrix operations     scalability Robust initialization: SVD-based initialization     fallback random orthogonal matrices Convergence guarantees: Monotonic improvement     configurable tolerance Key features: Vectorized operations using sparse matrix algebra Efficient projection onto orthogonal group O(d) Optional tightness certificate global optimality validation Flexible preprocessing multiple input formats

title: Graph Alignment by Spectral Corresponding Functions (GRASP) — grasp
text: core idea GRASP transfer functional maps 3D shape analysis graph alignment. Instead directly matching nodes (hard), matches functions defined nodes. finding robust mapping basis functions graph, GRASP deduces underlying node--node alignment -product. GRASP operates five conceptual blocks: Block : Spectral basis construction using eigendecomposition     graph Laplacians Block B: Multi-scale node descriptors using heat kernel     Personalized PageRank Block C: Base alignment using Stiefel manifold optimization Block D: Functional correspondence mapping Block E: Final node--node assignment via linear assignment algorithm provides global, multi-scale view graph structure robust noise structural perturbations. pairwise case, complexity dominated final assignment step (typically O(n³)). Key parameters: ncomp: Number eigenvectors used (dimension spectral basis) q_descriptors: Number descriptor functions multi-scale analysis sigma: Diffusion parameter controlling descriptor time scales lambda: Regularization balancing eigen-structure vs descriptor alignment

title: Graph Alignment by Spectral Corresponding Functions (GRASP) — grasp

Ovsjanikov, M., Ben-Chen, M., Solomon, J., Butscher, ., & Guibas, L. (2012). Functional maps: flexible representation maps shapes. ACM Transactions Graphics, 31(4), 1-11.

code: # \donttest{ # Example with hyperdesign graph data  # Create synthetic graph domains set.seed(123) domain1 <- list(   x = matrix(rnorm(100), 50, 2),  # Node features   design = data.frame(node_id = 1:50) ) domain2 <- list(   x = matrix(rnorm(100), 50, 2),   design = data.frame(node_id = 1:50)   )  # Create hyperdesign hd <- structure(list(domain1 = domain1, domain2 = domain2), class = "hyperdesign")  # Run GRASP alignment with default parameters result <- grasp(hd, ncomp = 20, q_descriptors = 50)  # Access alignment results node_assignment <- result$assignment aligned_embeddings <- result$s  # Use different parameters for robustness result_robust <- grasp(hd, ncomp = 30, sigma = 1.0, lambda = 0.2) # }  # \donttest{ # Example with hyperdesign graph data library(multidesign) library(tibble)  # Create synthetic graph domains (node coordinates for graph construction) set.seed(123) X1 <- matrix(rnorm(100), 50, 2)  # Node coordinates for domain 1 X2 <- matrix(rnorm(100), 50, 2)  # Node coordinates for domain 2  # Create design data frames with node indices (GRASP doesn't use features) design1 <- tibble(node_id = 1:50) design2 <- tibble(node_id = 1:50)  # Create multidesign objects md1 <- multidesign(X1, design1) md2 <- multidesign(X2, design2)  # Create hyperdesign from multidesign objects hd <- hyperdesign(list(domain1 = md1, domain2 = md2))  # Run GRASP alignment (purely spectral, uses graph structure from X) result <- grasp(hd, ncomp = 20, q_descriptors = 50) # }

title: Linear Similarity Embedding using Optimal Transport — linear_sim_embed
text: algorithm follows Linear Similarity Embedding Framework (SEF) Passalis & Tefas (2016). optimization uses either ADAM (R implementation) L-BFGS-B (C++ implementation). Similarities computed using Gaussian kernel: P_ij = exp(-||Y_i - Y_j||^2 / sigma_P). orthogonality penalty Jp = ||W'W - ||^2_F / (2*m^2). Key algorithmic features: Automatic sigma_P selection using histogram-spread heuristic (Step 2, Fig. 2) PCA/KPCA initialization faster convergence (Step 3, Fig. 2) Enforced similarity matrix symmetry numerical stability Alpha_p scheduling option improved convergence

title: Low-rank Alignment — lowrank_align
text: Low-rank alignment optimizes objective function Z = (1-μ) * M + 2μ * L M captures low-rank structure L graph Laplacian similarity matrix. method balances preserving low-rank structure (μ=0) enforcing similarity constraints (μ=1). **Semi-supervised Learning Support:** algorithm handles NA labels gracefully. Unlabeled samples: - Still contribute low-rank structure term M data - participate similarity constraints (L term) - Receive coordinates joint embedding space - Create isolated nodes produce zero eigenvalues (automatically   skipped) scale_M parameter controls whether apply eigenvalue-based scaling: - scale_M = FALSE (default): Uses original formulation   Z = (1-μ) * M + 2μ * L - scale_M = TRUE: Applies scaling M := M * (λ₁(L)/λ₁(M)), changing   objective scale_M = TRUE, mu parameter longer original mathematical meaning balancing two terms, relative scales artificially adjusted. reproducibility across different systems, set n_cores = 1 ensure deterministic results PRIMME eigenvalue computations. **Handling NA Labels:** Samples NA labels supported following mechanism: - contribute low-rank reconstruction term M = (-R)ᵀ(-R) - participate similarity constraints (zero rows/columns C) - create isolated nodes zero degree, producing zero eigenvalues - algorithm automatically detects skips zero modes - Final embedding includes coordinates samples (labeled unlabeled)

text: datasets list datasets. element must list fields `X` (n x 3 coordinates), `alpha` (length n masses), optional `F` (n x D features). template list fields `Y` (m x 3 coordinates), `beta` (length m masses), optional `G` (m x D features). omega Optional nonnegative weights datasets (length K). NULL, uses uniform weights. epsilon Entropic regularization parameter (> 0). rho1 KL penalty first marginal (> 0). rho2 KL penalty second marginal (> 0). lambda_anat Weight anatomical squared distance. lambda_feat Weight feature squared distance. neighbor_mode Neighborhood mode passed [uot_build_cost()]. k_neighbors Integer k kNN neighborhoods (used `"knn"` `"hybrid"` modes). radius Positive scalar radius `"radius"` / `"hybrid"` modes. maxk Maximum number candidate neighbors requested `"radius"` / `"hybrid"` mode (prevents quadratic blowups). min_neighbors Minimum number within-radius neighbors required per row `"hybrid"` mode falling back kNN. constraint_fields Optional character vector field names present dataset template define **hard transport constraints**. Edges allowed fields match (implemented via grouped neighbor search). Typical examples: `c("hemi")` `c("hemi","network")`. prior_fields Optional character vector field names present dataset template define **soft identity prior**. provided together `lambda_prior > 0`, dataset builds `prior_map` matching fields template adds soft bias term via [uot_build_cost()]. lambda_prior Nonnegative weight soft prior term. prior_sigma Optional positive scale prior term (units `template$Y`). dense_max_bytes Maximum dense cost size (bytes) allowed `neighbor_mode="auto"`. ensure_cols Logical; TRUE, adds reverse 1NN edges ensure every template column least one incoming edge (kNN/hybrid modes ). max_outer Maximum number template update iterations. max_inner Maximum number TI-Sinkhorn iterations per subject. tol_inner TI-Sinkhorn tolerance. tol_outer Template weight tolerance. rescale_pi2 scale subject's transported mass aggregating (`"alpha"` `"unit"`). target_mass Target total mass template weights. `"mean_alpha"`, uses mean subject mass; `"none"`, rescaling; numeric, uses . learn_template_features Logical; update template features `G`. delta Small stabilizer feature update denominators. parallel Logical; TRUE, uses `parallel::mclapply` Unix. ncores Number cores parallel subject solves. verbose Logical; print outer-loop progress.

title: Position-Aware Random Transport (PARROT) Network Alignment — parrot
text: PARROT tackles network alignment formulating regularized optimal transport problem. method incorporates position-aware features Random Walk Restart (RWR) descriptors enforces structural consistency neighborhood-preserving regularization terms. PARROT operates following algorithmic components: Position-Aware Features: Compute RWR descriptors capturing network position Cross-Network Cost: Build transport cost matrix networks Consistency Regularization: Add structural similarity constraints Optimal Transport: Solve regularized transport problem via Sinkhorn algorithm minimizes objective: $$L(S) = \langle C, S \rangle + \lambda_1 \Omega_1(S) + \lambda_2 \Omega_2(S) + \tau H(S)$$ \(C\) position-aware cost matrix, \(\Omega_1, \Omega_2\) consistency regularizers, \(H(S)\) entropy regularization term parameter \(\tau\). code: # \donttest{ # Example with hyperdesign network data  # Create synthetic network domains set.seed(123) domain1 <- list(   x = matrix(rnorm(200), 100, 2),  # Node features   design = data.frame(     node_id = 1:100,     anchors = c(1:10, rep(NA, 90))  # First 10 nodes are anchors   ) ) domain2 <- list(   x = matrix(rnorm(200), 100, 2),   design = data.frame(     node_id = 1:100,     anchors = c(1:10, rep(NA, 90))  # Corresponding anchors   ) )  # Create hyperdesign hd <- structure(list(domain1 = domain1, domain2 = domain2), class = "hyperdesign")  # Run PARROT alignment with default parameters result <- parrot(hd, anchors = anchors)  # Access alignment results transport_plan <- result$transport_plan aligned_embeddings <- result$s  # Use different regularization settings result_strong <- parrot(hd, anchors = anchors, lambda = 0.5, tau = 0.1) # }  # \donttest{ # Example with hyperdesign network data library(multidesign) library(tibble)  # Create synthetic network domains (node features for PARROT) set.seed(123) X1 <- matrix(rnorm(200), 100, 2)  # Node features for domain 1 X2 <- matrix(rnorm(200), 100, 2)  # Node features for domain 2  # Create design data frames with anchor correspondences (PARROT uses anchors) design1 <- tibble(   node_id = 1:100,   anchors = c(1:10, rep(NA, 90))  # First 10 nodes are anchors ) design2 <- tibble(   node_id = 1:100,   anchors = c(1:10, rep(NA, 90))  # Corresponding anchors )  # Create multidesign objects md1 <- multidesign(X1, design1) md2 <- multidesign(X2, design2)  # Create hyperdesign from multidesign objects hd <- hyperdesign(list(domain1 = md1, domain2 = md2))  # Run PARROT alignment (uses anchors from design component) result <- parrot(hd, anchors = anchors)  # Access alignment results transport_plan <- result$transport_plan aligned_embeddings <- result$s  # Use different regularization settings result_strong <- parrot(hd, anchors = anchors, lambda = 0.5, tau = 0.1) # }

text: pseudolabeling system addresses unsupervised domain adaptation identifying reliable correspondences samples different domains. approach uses similarity-based clustering, diversity-aware selection, adaptive thresholding, quality control filtering. Main functions: assign_pseudolabels(): General-purpose pseudolabeling     sparse similarity matrices high_sim_pseudolabels(): Specialized function     multi-domain data using cosine similarity create_synthetic_similarity_matrix(): Generate synthetic     data testing evaluate_pseudolabeling(): Evaluate pseudolabeling     performance ground truth Integration KEMA: Key parameters: sim_threshold: Controls similarities considered     "high". Can adaptive. diversity_weight: Balances cluster coherence vs.     representative diversity min_clusters/max_clusters: Controls number anchor     points min_cluster_size: Ensures clusters large enough     reliable

Use `NULL` auto-tune per domain via [choose_sigma()]. use_laplacian Logical; TRUE use normalized Laplacian bases. views Character vector view names `c("raw", "eigenmap", "hks")`. view_weights Optional numeric vector nonnegative weights, length `views` (normalized sum 1). k_embed Optional integer number eigenpairs used eigenmap/HKS. `NULL`, defaults `max(3*ncomp, ncomp + 10)` inside solver. hks_q Integer number HKS time steps. lambda_view Mix weight [0,1] view-distance vs token-OT cost. candidate_k Integer number ANN candidates per source node. ann_backend Nearest-neighbor backend candidate generation: `"auto"` (default), `"rann"`, `"annoy"` (requires RcppAnnoy). ann_trees Number trees used Annoy `ann_backend="annoy"`. prior_k Integer number candidates taken prior (reserved). ensure_cols Logical; ensure every target column least one incoming candidate edge (adds reverse-1NN edges needed). token_mode Either `"view_only"` (self token ) `"view_plus_neighbors"` (includes sampled neighbor tokens). max_hops Integer hop depth neighborhood tokens. samples_per_hop Integer number neighbors sampled per hop. max_tokens Maximum tokens retained per node (cap runtime). token_metric Token distance: `"cosine"` `"sqeuclidean"`. eps_token Entropic regularization token-level OT (>0). iters_token Maximum Sinkhorn iterations token-level OT. tol_token Token-level Sinkhorn convergence tolerance. eps_node Entropic regularization node-level sparse Sinkhorn (>0). iters_node Maximum iterations node-level sparse Sinkhorn. tol_node Node-level Sinkhorn convergence tolerance. projection Discrete projection mode: `"greedy"` `"hungarian"`. anchor_weight Nonnegative weight applied anchor mismatch penalty. anchor_penalty Nonnegative penalty added costs anchor mismatch edges endpoints anchored. seed Integer seed used randomized sampling. verbose Logical; print progress messages.
